findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is not set
findings.body: The query `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the `embed_category` site setting is non-empty and matches a category name. The default for `embed_category` is `''` (removed in this PR), so on a typical site the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. It should handle no result and skip directly to the uncategorized fallback.

findings.title: Migrated embeddable hosts are inserted without normalization, breaking existing allowed hosts
findings.body: Old `embeddable_hosts` accepted values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (the existing specs even use these), but the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares only `URI(...).host` to the stored `host` column. The migration inserts each old line verbatim, so rows containing a scheme or path will never match allowed-host checks after upgrade. Values are also interpolated directly into SQL; a host value containing a quote will break the migration or inject SQL. Normalize before insert and use parameterized queries.

findings.title: Update/destroy with missing record raises 500
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then pass the result to `save_host` or call `host.destroy` without checking for nil. A request for a non-existent id (stale admin tab, concurrent delete, or malformed request) will raise NoMethodError and return 500 instead of a JSON 404/error response. Use `find` or check `host.present?`.

findings.title: save_host assumes embeddable_host params are present
findings.body: `save_host` immediately accesses `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If `params[:embeddable_host]` is missing or null, this raises NoMethodError and returns 500. It should return a standard JSON validation error for missing parameters instead.

findings.title: before_validation does not handle nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called before validation on every save. If `host` is nil (for example from a direct model call or malformed API request), this raises NoMethodError rather than producing a normal validation error. Guard the normalization with `if self.host.present?` or add a presence validation before mutating.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
findings.body: The format validation explicitly allows an optional port (`:[0-9]{1,5}`), but `record_for_host` uses `uri.host` only and ignores `uri.port`. A configured host like `example.com:8080` will be compared as `example.com` and never match a referer to `http://example.com:8080/...`. Either reject ports in the validator or include `uri.port` in the comparison.

findings.title: Controller spec only checks inheritance
findings.body: The only test in this spec asserts that `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` subclasses `Admin::AdminController`; create, update, destroy, and `save_host` are untested. The missing-record and missing-param failure paths in this controller are exactly where bugs can land without coverage.
